sentences.text: It has been argued by learned counsel for the appellant that the appellant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
He would further submit that the there was friendship between the appellant and the victim/prosecutrix and she herself had gone with him to Indore and stayed there for several days.

He would next submit that the victim/prosecutrix is a consenting party and as per the MLC Report (Ex-P/22), she is habitual to physical relationship and FSL report (Ex-P/
32) is also negative.
He would next submit that except the Dakhil Kharij register, no other evidence has been brought by the prosecution to prove the age of the victim that she was minor on the date of incident.
The appellant is in jail since 03.6.2019, hence, he may be released on bail.
On the other hand, Shri Avinash Singh, learned counsel for the State opposes the prayer for grant of bail.

He would further submit that the appellant has enticed the minor girl, aged about 13 years and 6 months at the time of incident, took her to Indore, stayed there several days and also established physical relationship with her.
Hence, there is sufficient evidence against the appellant to connect him with crime in question.
Therefore, the appellant is not liable to be released on bail.
We have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the records of the Court below.

Taking into account the facts and circumstances of the case, particularly considering the act of the appellant, who took the minor prosecutrix, below the age of 16 years, to Indore and sexually exploited her for several days on the pretext of marriage, we are of the considered opinion that it is not a fit case to suspend the jail sentences.
Accordingly, IA No. 1 of 2023 stands rejected.
Let the matter be listed for final hearing after four weeks.

Sd/- Sd/-
 (NK Chandravanshi) (Ramesh Sinha)
 Judge Chief Justice Bini Ramu Yadav vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39743213/
